extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners developing or applying physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), e.g., computational scientists, applied mathematicians, and ML-for-PDE engineers
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and methodological criteria for building, training, validating, and deploying Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for solving forward/inverse PDE/SPDE problems, including data selection, loss design, architectures, optimization, software choices, and evaluation metrics. Emphasizes best practices, common pitfalls, and software features seen in the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training loss composition (initial, boundary, PDE residual, data)
rubrics_metrics.description: The training objective should include losses enforcing initial conditions, boundary conditions, and the PDE residual (collocation points); an optional data loss term can be included when supervised data are available (LB, LF, Ldata).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raissi et al. framework: explicitly minimize LB (initial+boundary) and LF (PDE residual on collocation points). Example: Ldata = 0 for a surrogate model trained only on initial data; design weights ω for combining multiple loss terms and monitor their relative magnitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and number of training points
rubrics_metrics.description: Training/collocation points may be arbitrarily distributed in the spatio-temporal domain; both the number and spatial/temporal placement of points strongly influence approximation quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increasing total points generally improves approximation, but location can be crucial. Sampling strategies discussed include equispaced (lattice-like), quasi-random Sobol sequences, and Latin hypercube sampling (Latin Hypercube used in examples). Example counts: N0 = 50 initial, Nb = 50 boundary, Nc = 20,000 collocation in the NLS benchmark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boundary condition enforcement: hard vs soft constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether to enforce boundary/initial conditions by embedding them directly in the network architecture (hard constraint/PCNN/trial function) or by penalizing violations via loss terms (soft constraint).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hard constraints can eliminate boundary loss terms but may be incompatible with arbitrary boundaries; soft constraints require appropriate weighting and complicate hyperparameter tuning. NeuroDiffEq enforces explicit constraints (PCNN) but may be inadequate for arbitrary boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaling, non-dimensionalization and normalization of inputs/parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Address disparate magnitudes of physical parameters and inputs via non-dimensionalization and normalization to improve training and stability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kissas et al. used non-dimensionalization/normalization to mitigate issues arising from different parameter scales; perform preprocessing to make learning feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptive residual-based refinement (RAR) of collocation points
rubrics_metrics.description: Iteratively add collocation points in regions where the PDE residual is large until a mean-residual threshold is achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RAR is analogous to FEM adaptive refinement: identify high-residual regions during training and concentrate collocation points there to improve local accuracy (supported in DeepXDE).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimizer selection and training schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose optimizers and schedules (e.g., Adam for initial training then L-BFGS for fine-tuning), appropriate learning rates, and possible learning-rate annealing or weight-adaptation schemes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical strategy: Adam with lr=1e-3 followed by L-BFGS fine-tune. Modulus uses global learning-rate annealing; TensorDiffEq implements Self-Adaptive PINN to increase weights for larger loss components. Monitor convergence and consider hybrid optimizer schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loss weighting and dynamic/adaptive weighting strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Because multiple loss terms are combined (PDE residual, BCs, data), weights must be chosen or adapted during training to balance objectives and avoid domination by one term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use global annealing or adaptive weight-update rules (e.g., self-adaptive PINN) to increase weights corresponding to larger losses. Improper weighting complicates hyperparameter tuning and can hinder convergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics and error reporting (MSE, MAE, relative L2, training loss)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report standard error metrics such as mean squared error (MSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and relative L2 norm, alongside training losses, to quantify approximation quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide spatial/temporal error maps and snapshot comparisons to benchmarks; the paper reports MSE/MAE and local peak errors (e.g., MSE ~5.17e-04 in an example). Use multiple metrics for a full picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation against high-fidelity benchmark solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate PINN predictions by comparison to high-resolution numerical solutions (e.g., spectral solvers, Chebfun) or experimental data where available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate reference solutions with trusted numerical methods and compare spatially and temporally (snapshots, error maps) to detect systematic failures (e.g., difficulty around symmetric peaks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Network architecture design appropriate to the PDE
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose network inputs, outputs, depth, width, and activation functions in accordance with problem structure (e.g., real+imaginary outputs for complex-valued PDEs, periodic BCs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for 1D NLS use 2 inputs (t,x), output length 2 (real and imaginary parts), 5 layers × 100 neurons, tanh activation. Explore architectures and report how MAE/MSE change across configurations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of function representation / specialized architectures
rubrics_metrics.description: Select architectures tailored for the task: Fourier networks for oscillatory solutions, DGM/LSTM-like for certain PDEs, DeepONet/DeepM&Mnet for operator learning and multiscale problems, encoder–decoder for image-to-field inversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modulus supports Fourier Networks and DGM; DeepONet is suited for operator approximation across parameterized families and multi-physics/multi-scale tasks. Match architecture to feature types (periodicity, multiscale, operator mapping).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulation of PDE residual/loss: strong vs weak forms and integral vs summation
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether to enforce PDEs in their strong form (pointwise residuals) or weak/variational form and whether to compute losses via pointwise summation or integral formulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modulus implements an integral formulation rather than pointwise summation and supports strong or weak forms; choice affects numerical properties and solver capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling strategy selection (equispaced, Sobol, Latin Hypercube)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a sampling method for collocation and data points that suits the problem (regular grids, quasi-random low-discrepancy sequences, or Latin hypercube).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pang et al. studied lattice/equispaced sampling; Sobol and Latin hypercube sequences are common quasi-random choices; Latin Hypercube was used in several examples to generate training points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capability to infer latent/unobserved state variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Use PINNs to recover unobserved or latent state variables from partial/noisy measurements by incorporating the governing PDE constraints into learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zhang et al. observed that PINNs can accurately predict missing variables; design training to leverage available measurements plus physics to infer latent fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extrapolation and temporal projection robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the PINN's ability to project solutions beyond the time window used during training; vanilla PINNs may perform poorly on temporal extrapolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test extrapolation explicitly (projecting in time) since many PINNs fail to generalize beyond training time. Consider specialized architectures or training approaches for extrapolation tasks (Kim et al. provide alternatives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling noisy measurements and uncertainty quantification
rubrics_metrics.description: When data are noisy, incorporate noise-aware methods and perform uncertainty quantification (e.g., approximate Bayesian computation, sequential Monte Carlo) to obtain posterior distributions over model parameters or fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cavanagh et al. used KDE to convert embeddings to PDFs and then fitted a Fokker–Planck model with PINNs, using ABC-SMC to obtain posterior parameter densities; embed noise models and UQ where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-fidelity and surrogate modeling for computational efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploit multi-fidelity data (few high-fidelity simulations + many cheap approximations) to build efficient surrogate PINNs that generalize across parameter spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPINN estimated nano-fluid viscosity using a small number of molecular dynamics simulations; design multi-fidelity architectures to leverage scarce expensive data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loss design aligned to measurement/observation space
rubrics_metrics.description: Define loss functions consistent with how measurements are obtained (e.g., compute loss in scatter space for scattering-image inversion rather than object space), and add auxiliary losses (e.g., binary loss) to enforce physical constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stielow & Scheel compute scatter-space MSE and apply binary loss to enforce physical binary nature; tailor losses to the measurement transform for better reconstruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software/toolbox feature checklist for PINN development
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate PINN libraries by feature support: boundary-condition handling (hard/soft), geometry capabilities (CSG, tessellated geometry), adaptive residual refinement, supported NN architectures, scalability/distributed computing, optimizer integrations, and active maintenance/community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: DeepXDE supports RAR and CSG; Modulus supports integral loss formulations, CSG/TG, many NN types and global learning-rate annealing; NeuroDiffEq enforces hard BCs; TensorDiffEq targets distributed computing and self-adaptive weighting. Consider available example problems and ongoing development when selecting a package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualization and diagnostic practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Use spatial/temporal error maps, snapshots at multiple times, and pointwise error analyses to diagnose where the PINN succeeds or fails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plot predicted vs benchmark solutions at key time slices, error heatmaps, and track how error grows over time; identify local peak errors and symmetry/failure patterns (e.g., difficulty mapping central peak or symmetric intervals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of PINN limitations and appropriate problem selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize problem classes where PINNs may struggle (multi-scale, chaotic, turbulent, or specially-tailored PDEs) and compare against traditional numerical methods which may be superior for certain PDEs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors caution that PINNs can fail to learn complex physical phenomena and may be outperformed by PDE-specific numerical solvers; perform feasibility checks and consider hybrid or problem-specific alternatives.
